📋 **Planning: 1 level first person shooter game**

*For a 1 level first-person shooter game — move and hide, I need to establish the core game loop, input handling, and basic scene rendering. The game should have a level with an exit point and a player that can move and hide from a basic AI. The game loop is the heart of the game, where input is processed and the scene is rendered. I need to ensure we have a clear, structured data model for the game state, input handling, and scene rendering.*

**Files to create:**
  `1. src/game.ts` — Game loop and state management (typescript)
  `2. src/input.ts` — Input handling for player movement and interaction (typescript)
  `3. src/scene.ts` — Scene rendering and collision detection (typescript)
  `4. src/game.ts` — Game loop and state management (typescript)
  `5. index.html` — Single self-contained GUI page (HTML + CSS + JS inline, no build step) that renders the complete app interface and wires it to the logic. This is what makes the app viewable in the browser preview — build the full UI here. STRICT RULES: (1) do NOT reference external files — no <script src="...">, no <link href="...">, no CSS or JS files; the preview iframe cannot load external files, so inline ALL CSS in a <style> tag and ALL JavaScript in a <script> tag directly in this file; (2) plain browser JavaScript only — no React, no TypeScript, no imports, no JSX, no build step; (3) include working inline code that actually renders the interface so the page is never blank. (html)
